input.standard: NASA analog habitat scrubber test protocols; MathWorks system identification overview
input.purpose: Commissioning dimensioning test: identify scrubber gain, efficiency and response time across the operator's requested 30-100% motor speed envelope using observed motor speed and simulated cabin CO2 response.
hypotheses: Single-pass removal efficiency (inlet/outlet CO2 difference) is not measured; the logger provides only cabin concentrations.
Electrical efficiency (motor current vs duty) is not measured; no current channel is logged.
Inter-module exchange through the hatch is not independently established by the closed-hatch logger; Hab-B CO2 response reflects coupled dynamics.
The scrubber's internal lag (tau) is not uniquely identified from cabin CO2 alone; the fitted response time constant represents effective cabin behaviour under stated assumptions.

monitoring.reason: Occupants of the volume under test; air changes during the test expose them.

steps.why: First operator-requested plateau; 6 sim minutes at 2x clock gives 12 wall-clock seconds, meeting the 10-second filming requirement.
Second operator-requested plateau; same dwell justification.
Third operator-requested plateau; same dwell justification.
Fourth operator-requested plateau; same dwell justification.
Fifth operator-requested plateau; same dwell justification.
Sixth operator-requested plateau; same dwell justification.
Seventh operator-requested plateau; same dwell justification.
Eighth operator-requested plateau; same dwell justification. Total 48 sim minutes < 60-minute ceiling.

expected.motor_speed: Observed speed_percent plateaus at each commanded 30,40,50,60,70,80,90,100% with at least 10 wall-clock seconds per plateau.
expected.co2_response: Lab CO2 (co2_lab_ppm) shows a measurable response to each speed step; Hab-B CO2 (co2_habb_ppm) shows coupled response. The transient shape and endpoint change across steps estimate scrubber gain (K) and effective time constant (tau) under the first-order hypothesis tau*dy/dt + y = K*u.
expected.identification_scope: Parameters fixed from documentation: flow 3.3 m3/min, efficiency 0.30, lag ~3.3 min (scrubber-1-datasheet). Parameters estimated from cabin response: effective gain and time constant, with stated assumptions (coupled mass balance, no independent inlet/outlet measurement). Residuals, uncertainty and competing explanations (exchange, mixing, sensor dynamics) reported.

justifications.reason: Operator's explicit acquisition requirement: 6 simulated minutes per plateau at 2 wall-clock seconds per simulated minute yields 12 wall-clock seconds, satisfying the 10-second minimum filming requirement; 8 plateaus total 48 sim minutes, below the 60-minute ceiling.

input.summary: The commissioning dimensioning procedure for the CO2 scrubber has been accepted by the guard. It defines an ascending staircase test at 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, and 100 percent motor speed, with 6 simulated minutes (12 wall-clock seconds) dwell at each plateau, within the 60-minute ceiling. All safety constants verified: CO2 abort ceiling 3100 ppm, speed floor 30%, max test duration 60 minutes, heart rate band 45-120 bpm, battery abort at 35%. The procedure uses observed telemetry channels (motor speed percent, CO2 concentrations) and respects the simulated environment. Scientific officer approval recorded; commander launch authorisation would be next but is outside this scoped mission.
